title: When Agents Play Differently: Localizing Human--Agent Behavioral Divergence with Conditional Distributional Testing
abstract: arXiv:2611.26012v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Evaluating whether artificial agents behave like humans requires comparing not just average outcomes but entire behavioral distributions across diverse contexts. We propose a stratified framework that computes nonparametric discrepancy statistics within contextual cells, and discovers subgroup rules identifying where agent behavior departs from human play. We show that session-level metrics dominated by win/loss outcomes offer little signal beyond mean comparisons, whereas process-level metrics such as move efficiency reveal genuine behavioral differences. Applied to a commercial match-3 game, it uncovers patterns invisible to aggregate metrics: a playtesting bot is diverging substantially from humans in certain game modes, while showing no detectable divergence in others. We release our implementation as open source to support reproducibility and adoption.

translated_title: 当智能体表现不同时：利用条件分布检验定位人类与智能体的行为差异
translated_abstract: 评估人工智能智能体是否表现得像人类，不仅需要比较平均结果，还需要在多样化情境中比较完整的行为分布。我们提出了一个分层框架，在情境单元内计算非参数差异统计量，并通过发现子群规则来识别智能体行为在哪些方面偏离了人类玩法。我们证明，由胜负结果主导的对局级指标除了均值比较之外几乎不提供额外信号，而走子效率等过程级指标则能揭示真实的行为差异。将该框架应用于一款商业三消游戏，它揭示了聚合指标无法察觉的模式：一个游戏测试机器人在某些游戏模式中与人类存在显著差异，而在其他模式中未检测到明显分歧。我们开源发布了该实现，以支持可复现性和推广使用。
tldr: 提出了一种基于分层条件分布检验的框架，利用情境单元内的非参数差异统计量和子群规则精确定位智能体与人类行为产生分歧的具体场景，并在商业三消游戏中发现了聚合指标无法察觉的模式级行为差异。
en_tdlr: Proposes a stratified framework that uses nonparametric discrepancy statistics within contextual cells and subgroup rule discovery to localize where agent behavior diverges from human play, revealing mode-level behavioral differences in a commercial match-3 game that aggregate metrics cannot detect.
